title: Quarter Navigation and Transformation Task Practice
description: Practice reading bearings, choosing triangle strategies, and applying coordinate transformation rules.

questions.question: A bearing of 090° points in which direction?
questions.explanation: Bearings are measured clockwise from north. A 090° bearing points east.

questions.question: A bearing of 180° points in which direction?
questions.explanation: A 180° clockwise turn from north points south.

questions.question: A route has two known legs and the included angle between them. Which strategy is usually best for finding the direct distance between the start and end points?
questions.explanation: Two sides and the included angle form an SAS case, which usually points to the Law of Cosines.

questions.question: A boat travels on a bearing of 040° to point B, then turns to a bearing of 130° to point C. What is the back bearing from B to the starting point?
questions.explanation: The back bearing is 180° opposite the original bearing: 040° + 180° = 220°.

questions.question: A point P(2, -3) is translated by the rule (x, y) -> (x + 5, y - 1). Write the image point P'.
questions.explanation: Add 5 to the x-coordinate and subtract 1 from the y-coordinate: P'(7, -4).

questions.question: Which coordinate rule translates every point 4 units left and 6 units up?
questions.explanation: Left decreases x by 4, and up increases y by 6.

questions.question: Reflect A(-6, 4) across the y-axis. Write the image point A'.
questions.explanation: Reflection across the y-axis changes x to its opposite and keeps y the same.

questions.question: Rotate Q(3, 8) 90° counterclockwise about the origin. Write the image point Q'.
questions.explanation: A 90° counterclockwise rotation uses (x, y) -> (-y, x), so Q'( -8, 3 ).

questions.question: When transforming a mapped route, the same coordinate rule should be applied to every route point.
questions.explanation: Applying the same rule to every point preserves the intended transformation of the whole route.

questions.question: In one or two sentences, explain why drawing a north reference line at each turn helps in a bearing problem.
questions.correctAnswer: A bearing is measured clockwise from north, so a north reference line at each turn gives the correct starting direction for the next angle. It helps prevent mixing bearings with standard coordinate angles.
questions.explanation: The key idea is that every bearing starts from north at the point where the direction is being measured.
